pairs.subject: agent-host-experience
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/app-master/backbone.ts:387 kp hands long-running App-master work to the Personas agent. When a rollup leaves out `ledgerConsistent`, `backboneFromRollup` sets it to `true`, and the ledger rule (scored as measured, line 271ff) then credits the full weight on a self-report the delegate never made. So a gap in the delegate's claim about its own work reaches the roster verdict as a pass, even though the report parser does treat the payload as untrusted input (report-payload.ts:34).

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/app-master/backbone.ts:387 Here kp is the delegating side. The technique says a delegate's completion is a claim to check, not believe. The parser does bound the payload as untrusted (report-payload.ts:34: 'nothing in it is trusted beyond its shape'). But a missing ledger self-report is filled in as 'consistent' and scored as measured, and a missing forbiddenClassViolations count becomes 0, so the forbidden-class gate passes. The verdict therefore rests on the delegate's own word, with silence counted as success.

app/_lib/agent-hire/lifecycle.ts:100 No task starts in an outside assistant here. kp calls Personas, and the human approval happens in Personas; kp records the request as pending, not done. This is not a hand-off from a host back into the product.

pairs.registryProposal: peer-agent-delegation's 'The product as the delegating side' section could name the case where the delegate's report is the only evidence of its own work (a self-reported ledger or violation count). It should say that a field the delegate did not send is unmeasured, never filled with the passing value.

pairs.evidence: app/_lib/tasks.ts:47 This is an in-process background job queue whose progress the tasks dock reads by polling the settled DB row (task-poll-state.ts:80, POLL_ACTIVE_MS). It is not an agent front end streaming run events, and it is not a tool surface for outside agents: a search of app/_lib for mcp, text/event-stream, structuredContent and tools/list found no hits.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/task-poll-state.ts:80 The runs are batch pipeline jobs that the UI polls; there is no agent turn with text deltas, tool calls or consent events for several surfaces to read. That matches the technique's own 'when not to use' clause.
app/_lib/tasks.ts:47 The task engine exposes no operations to outside agents. The only client is kp's own UI, which reads the task row.
